full_judgment: 7. Mr. Nuro Nabi, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the Courts below misread and misconstrued the evidence on record and thereby committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in decreeing the suit. He next submits that both the Courts below failed to appreciate that the unregistered sale deed alleged to have been executed in favour of the vendors of the plaintiffs was a forged and an antedated one and the Courts below decreed the suit by putting reliance on the said forged deeds. He also points out that the plaintiff could not prove his possession on the suit land but on the other hand, the defendants by adducing evidence proved their possession on the suit land and the Courts below failed to appreciate that the defendants are claiming the suit land by way of inheritance and the S.A. and R.S. records in the name of the plaintiff are not the exclusive proof of possession and thus it cannot be the basis for deciding the matter in question. He also submits that for ends of justice, the matter may be referred to the trial Court for rehearing on remand. He submits that the suit land was not properly demarcated by metes and bounds and no order of injunction can be passed on an unspecified land. In support to his contention the learned Advocate has referred a decision as reported in 50 D.L.R.(AD) page 188. He also points out that during the pendency of the present revision another title suit being Title suit No.35 of 2006 was filed before the Senior Assistant Judge. Munshiganj under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act for recovery of khas possession regarding the selfsame suit land, Which is fixed for preemptory hearing. The learned Advocate for the petitioners referred some decisions in support to his contentions made before this Court as reported in 50 D.L.R.(AD) page 188, 50 D.L.R.(H.C,) page 271, 39 D.L.R.(H.C.) page 8. He submits that section 9 of the Specific Relief Act does not authorise the Court to order for demolishing or removing dwelling huts or other permanent structures in the suit land while effecting restoration of possession. In support to his contention the learned Advocate has referred a decision as reported in 50 D.L.R.(H.C.) page-271. He next submits that when a person is dispossessed from any immovable property, he may file a suit to recover possession thereof, and the question of title will not be a matter of decision in that suit and under the provision of section 9 of the Specific Relief Act removal of structures raised by the defendant on the property cannot be ordered. In support to his contention the learned Advocate has referred a decision as reported in 39 D.L.R.(H.C.) page 8. The learned Advocate submits that during the pendency of the present Civil Revision the petitioner got possession on the suit land and made structures on it which cannot be removed now.
